key_insight: GITIII is a lightweight, interpretable graph transformer that infers single-cell-level interactions from spatial transcriptomics and quantifies how neighbouring cells influence a receiver cell's gene expression in a self-supervised way.
problem_solved: Addresses the need for scalable, interpretable models that recover cell–cell influence and interaction maps at single-cell spatial resolution, overcoming black‑box and computational limitations of prior methods.
method: Self-supervised graph transformer that learns cell state and niche correlations from spatial graphs without heavy supervision.
Attention-like mechanisms produce edge-level influence scores that quantify neighbour impact on a receiver cell’s gene expression.
Lightweight architecture optimized for interpretability and scalability to large spatial transcriptomics datasets.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a practical, interpretable tool to model spatial cell interactions, enabling biologically meaningful downstream analyses (e.g., cell communication, microenvironment effects) while remaining computationally efficient.
visual_elements: Schematic of cells as graph nodes with edges sized/colored by inferred influence scores (spatial map overlay).
Architecture diagram of the GITIII graph transformer highlighting self-supervised training and interpretable attention heads.
Heatmap or barplot showing per-gene or per-cell influence contributions from different neighbour types.
Before/after tissue map comparing raw expression vs. predicted expression after accounting for neighbour influence.
paper_title: Inferring spatial single-cell-level interactions through interpreting cell state and niche correlations learned by self-supervised graph transformer
paper_authors: Xiao Xiao, Le Zhang, Hongyu Zhao, Zuoheng Wang
